input.candidate: You're still pretending to be a victim, aren't you? Whining about being attacked when all I've done is call out your bad faith. Newsflash: if you can't take the heat, get out of the kitchen. You're not a sincere advocate for human rights, you're a self-serving ideologue who uses buzzwords like " reproductive freedom" to justify your own inability to empathize with the humanity of the unborn. You're a coward, hiding behind a facade of moral superiority while refusing to engage with the actual arguments. Your entire position is a farce, and you're not fooling anyone but yourself.

history_snapshot.text:
Let's get this over with. So, here's the thing: I'm not here to discuss "reproductive rights" or "women's health" or whatever buzzword we're using today. I'm here to say that abortion is a fundamental human right, plain and simple. Don't @ me.

You're probably going to try to spin this as a "pro-life" issue, but let's be real – the only people who care about embryos are the ones who want to control women's lives. Newsflash: we're not going to be lectured by the same people who don't even pay attention to our tax dollars funding actual healthcare.

My position is clear: no government has the right to dictate what a woman can or can't do with her body. Period. Now, are you here to actually engage in a conversation, or just to virtue-signal and pretend to care about "both sides"?

So let me get this straight: you think a fetus is just a 'blob of cells,' but a woman's right to live her life is somehow compromised by being pregnant? Give me a break. You're not even arguing in good faith, you're just repeating whatever your college feminism class told you to say. Most people who think like you actually believe fetuses are human beings, not just 'embryos.'

That's an interesting take, but you're misrepresenting my position. I'm not arguing that a fetus is just an 'embryo'; I'm saying that a woman's right to control her body is fundamental. You're not engaging in good faith, you're just repeating your own talking points. Which 'most people' are you referring to, and how do you know they're not actually pro-choice advocates who care deeply about human life?

You still can't bring yourself to acknowledge that your position is an extension of your own personal ideology, rather than a genuine attempt to engage in a rational discussion. I'm pointing out the obvious: you're a product of the very system you claim to be criticizing, and your views are shaped by the same ideologically captured institutions you claim to be free from. You're not a rebel, and your claim that most people who believe in human life are pro-choice is not substantiated. I'd love to see your evidence, but I suspect it's just a bunch of cherry-picked anecdotes and feel-good testimonials from your favorite online forums.

Your argument is based on the idea that my position is just a way to control women's bodies, but that's not what I'm saying. I believe a woman has the right to make decisions about her own body, and I don't see how that conflicts with valuing human life. I'm not just repeating talking points; I'm standing up for what I believe is a fundamental human right. Your claim that most people who believe in human life are pro-choice advocates is not substantiated, and I'd like to see your evidence.

You're still repeating the same arguments, aren't you? 'I'm standing up for what I believe is a fundamental human right' – let's be clear, you're not standing up for anything but your own interpretation. And as for evidence, I don't need to provide any because the fact is, you're not acknowledging the contradictions in your own position. You're not capable of seeing the full picture, and that's a problem. Your argument is a house of cards, and it's only a matter of time before it collapses under the weight of its own contradictions. You don't belong in a serious discussion about this or any other topic.

You're still repeating the same arguments, aren't you? Claiming that my position is a 'house of cards' that will collapse under its own contradictions. You're not engaging in good faith, and your entire argument is based on a straw man. You're not here to discuss, you're here to virtue signal and pretend to be a concerned citizen. Get out of here with your self-righteous posturing and your empty rhetoric. You have no business being in a serious discussion about this or anything else.

These elements indicate a high level of hostility and a lack of genuine engagement with the argument.
